Inputs MUST be grouped under headings in this order: Implementation, for sources reached by an `{impl}` edge from the definition, including anchored files; Tests, for sources reached by a `{test}` edge, including tests, examples, and anchored files; Referenced definitions, for declarations the definition cites and their terminology; and Other sources, for the remaining inputs the assessment consulted. Edges MUST be determined from the current references under {cite}`requirements.references.targets` and {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. A requirements input MUST show its selection and each matched definition's full name, file, and inclusive line range. Each subsection MUST show the exact recorded text in a fenced code block. **Verdict:** The detail-page implementation is mostly complete and well tested. Two gaps remain, and neither has a FIXME acknowledging it. **What is covered** - `render_detail_sections` and `render_detail_page` in `src/index.rs` produce: - the state badge; - the `## Requirement` or `## Example` block quote of the current definition text; - the `## Rationale` section, with "No rationale recorded." as the fallback; - the `## FIXME references` section, fed by `LoadedDetailEvidence::load`, `fixme_entries` and `Judgment::fixme_entries`; - the `## Inputs` section. - `InputGroup`, `heading`, `id`, `DefinitionEdges::current` and `DefinitionEdges::group` implement the four groups in the required order. - Edges come from current `{impl}` and `{test}` reference sites, from anchors (via `complete_file`), and from the definition's `{cite}` roles. - Groups are `
` and inputs are `
` (collapsed). - `render_input`, `render_source_location` and `InputLocation::resolve` give each input its own selector label and its resolved file and inclusive line range. For requirements inputs, they also give each matched definition's name. - `push_code_block` and `code_language` select the fence languages: `rust,noplayground`, markdown, json, ini for TOML, java, javascript, typescript, python. - Tests: - `detail_page_renders_markdown_and_highlighted_input_sections` covers the badge URL, block quote, Rationale, input summary and fence languages. - `common_input_extensions_select_highlighting_languages` covers the remaining languages. - `detail_inputs_are_grouped_by_current_edges_in_disclosures` covers group order and membership, anchors, `{cite}`, disclosure counts and open/closed state. - `index_lists_examples_and_links_their_detail_pages` covers the example label. - `valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book` in `tests/outcomes.rs` covers FIXME display. **Gaps** 1. **Unmarked implementation of the alt-text obligation.** The "Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text" is actually produced by `shield_badge` in `src/lib.rs`, which builds the ``. That function is marked `{impl}` only for `requirements.references.book_badges` and `requirements.references.safe_badges`, not for `requirements.index.detail_format`. `render_detail_sections` only supplies the label, message and colour. Code that implements part of the requirement without an `{impl}` reference is a gap. 2. **Alt text is not tested for detail pages.** - The detail-page tests assert only the badge URL substring (`img.shields.io/badge/evidence-Valid-237346`). - The `alt="evidence …"` assertions I found in `src/lib.rs` cover the `req`/`example` book badges, not the detail-page badge. - There is also no detail-page test that puts an input selected by a `definition` selector, such as terminology, into the "Referenced definitions" group. That is a smaller gap.

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST NOT be counted as additional source references.
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one project file path per option line. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`, from the definition to the complete
anchored file, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
An anchored file MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
complete file, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path that does
not resolve to a readable, permitted file MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such
as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the
definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
